content.title: Jinn, Magic & the Evil Eye
content.subtitle: Know the Signs and the Right Way to Protect Yourself
content.body:
“From the next day, he developed a severe fever and chills, almost leading to pneumonia. Yet just the day before, a father had thought, ‘My child hasn’t been sick for so long. Look how cheerful and full of life he is!’”

Have you ever experienced something like this?

One brother shared that whenever a relative visited his friend’s home, his child would fall sick the next day. Another said he told his wife, “Our little one is eating well.” From the next day, the child stopped wanting to eat.

A third brother said, “I’ve had the same experience! That day, I was thinking, ‘My child hasn’t been sick for so long. Just looking at him makes my heart happy.’” Yet the next day, the child developed fever and chills, almost leading to pneumonia.

The Evil Eye: Mere Coincidence or a Serious Reality?

Many of us dismiss such incidents as “coincidences” or psychological misconceptions. Yet in Islam, the evil eye is not imaginary. It is a truth. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:

“The evil eye is real. If anything could precede the divine decree, it would be the evil eye.”

— Sahih Muslim: 2188

It is not only an envious person’s gaze that can cause harm. If we look at our children, family, career, or achievements with admiration without remembering Allah, we may unknowingly become affected by the evil eye ourselves.

How Can You Protect Your Family from Invisible Harm?

Spiritual afflictions such as the evil eye, jinn, and magic affect countless families. Sometimes, no physical illness is found, yet distress and unexplained disruption enter life. To ensure spiritual safety, we need knowledge of authentic Shar‘i Ruqyah and its methods.
